findings.status: fixed (redesign); residual risk = scaled glide/reefing, disclosed
findings.changed: Aero rebuilt on ONE coupled polar per canopy (model.js polar/makePolarTable). Soft wing anchored to NASA TN D-4182/D-4672 (L/D ≤1 only at CR ≥0.8, collapse <22.5°, no inflation >75°); it is kept only as comparison design 4. K2-R uses a statically stable slotted round canopy (L/D = Gmax·u, CD0 0.80) with pull set by skirt reefing (drag area 1→0.25, Knacke/Ares data) and a gust-absorbing winch; collapse on slack line / wing α boundaries modelled.
findings.remaining: Passes only if the 0.7 m canopy with pod glides at ≥≈0.9–1.0 (MC-6 range) and keeps ≥40 % of its glide when reefed; at MC-1-1C's 0.75 the ensemble fails KE (19.7 J). Tow-test polar (glide vs slot opening × reef) is the decisive gate.

findings.changed: Flying mass built with components.js budget() + canopy at Skytex 27 g/m² ×1.3 + 15 % margin (kiteBudget), 4 g servos (shared 2.5 g class is too weak), 1.2 Wh cell; worn mass recomputed; KE gate enforced by a dock-above-14.6 m/s rule.

budget: ASSUMED (4–5 g digital micro servo class); shared 2.5 g servo is too weak for 20–40 % of a 6–25 N line load (audit K2-02)

findings.changed: Launch interlock: armed AND descending >0.3 m/s AND on-snow vibration signature AND rider speed window; any 3 m climb auto-disarms (so the arm tap at the top is the 1 action per run). Scenarios chairlift (5 m/s up) and chairdown (5 m/s down) added.

findings.changed: 0.35 m folding exit mast (line exit ≈1.9 m upright), hi-vis sheath, line-contact detection (60 ms) → 1.5 N free-spool and flag; snag → free-spool → pack release; new crosspole scenario (forced contact at 2.3 m).
findings.remaining: At carved-turn apex the body (and mast) lean puts the line 0.9–1.5 m above snow 1 m behind; not fixable by mast length. Forced contact still 16.6 N for ≈60 ms (target ≤10 N). Envelope: nobody within ~5 m behind, low-traffic runs.

findings.changed: Documented as a gate in modelLimits/design_notes; exposure minimised (auto-dock at every stop, never launches on lifts, dock above 14.6 m/s).

findings.remaining: Envelope: tailwind ≤6 m/s at 12 m/s riding (≈0.5 × rider speed).

audit2.basis: shared re-audit rules (common/fullrun.js availMask, footageStability jitter p90, simulated setup, ops p90 + max, windEstimate gates; criteria.js headClear); 39-case ensemble regenerated; independent recompute from raw columns on 6 spot cases (results.json independent)
audit2.summary: All 13 judged metrics pass on the shared basis at the documented L/D 0.75 with half the glide kept when reefed: avail 81.52 % (p10 76.02), jitter p90 1.66 °/s, setup p90 4.7 s, ops p90 1 (max 1), body force 28.14 N (raw 50 ms), KE 12.92 J, endurance 56.94 min (48.46 without regeneration credit), headClear ≥1.1 m, azRange 58.14°. KE, body force and head clearance no longer depend on L/D, reefed glide or mass (sensitivities); avail does (tailwind envelope). Line/boom height behind the rider is NOT fixed.

findings.changed: Root cause measured: the KE peaks were body-roll yanks of the exit in hockey stops (exit 8–9 m/s relative to the CoM → kite 17–18.5 m/s) and, at L/D 0.75, crosswind azimuth blow-out. Now: heave-compensating winch + KE governor (soft clutch above √(2·12.5 J/m) of the actual mass, reel-in capped by the KE limit), fast reel-in on braking, glide default 0.75 (MC-1-1C).

findings.status: fixed by geometry + procedure (residual: trumpet capture untested)
findings.changed: The boom is pointed at the kite (line-aligned), so the KCU arrives on the boom axis whenever the line is inside the gimbal cone; the tip trumpet only takes the residual (45°). Retrieval starts at hockey-stop detection and reels in fast while the apparent wind is still from ahead, so the kite docks before the rider stops. Standing stows: face the wind (kite behind); wrong facing → head interlock snaps it onto the tip, +1 hand action.

Never re-inflated on snow (reeled in and docked or hand-stowed), launch released reefed (≤4 N steady) from the extended boom with a 6·D0 filling time and a 1.8 opening-shock factor, body force judged on the raw 50 ms mean at the integration step.

findings.status: NOT fixed — mitigated and bounded; envelope limit
findings.changed: Line now leaves a 1.2 m hi-vis boom (exit 0.7 m above the pack); rear proximity radar softens the clutch (1.5 N) and climbs the kite; line contact force and boom contact impulse reported. Carving inclination keeps the boom/line 0.8–1.3 m above the snow 1 m behind the rider; the boom itself is now the obstacle nearest the body.

findings.status: dependence removed for safety metrics; bounded for avail

availMask; jitter = p90 of footageStability subjectRms (all flown cases); ops p90 + max; setup simulated (reel-in over snow and walk to a rag at 1 m/s simulated; hand time 8 s ASSUMED); windEstimate for launch/stop/park gates (in-flight control on the KCU pitot); headClear judged; heater over the whole day; mass incl. omitted hardware.

Iteration 2 did not count its 0.35 m mast as footage artefact; a rigid exit near the rider is always in the shot from the line end. Passive (line-aligned) boom → art >3 % in ≈45–55 % of frames; only active pointing at the camera keeps it end-on.

Envelope results: below ≈7 m/s apparent wind the kite does not launch (shorttail: 0 % avail); a rider accelerating past ≈16 m/s outruns the KE-capped dock (fast: KE transient); winch-motor failure at a stop leaves the line within 0.8 m of the helmet; the boom is hit at shoulder height by a skier crossing 0.35 m behind.

killTests: Tow/car-top test of the 0.40 m² slotted round + KCU at 6–15 m/s: L/D vs slot opening unreefed (kill if <0.6: avail 73.02 % at 0.6) and at reef 0.25/0.35/0.5 (kill if retention <0.3 or coning >10°).

Heave-compensation winch bench: replay the measured hockey-stop exit motion (8–9 m/s, 0.4 s) on a moving anchor with a 90 g dummy: kill if the dummy ground speed exceeds √(2·14.9 J/m) or the winch lag >30 ms.
Governor: 2 N soft clutch at 7 m line; drogue deceleration on the soft line within 0.3 s.
Boom: 1.2 m telescopic on a 2-axis gimbal pointing at a moving target with ≤0.5° error at 20 Hz under carving vibration, 0.13 N·m gravity load; real footage artefact <3 % of subject height.
Dock: 500 seats onto the boom-tip trumpet at ≤45° residual (wet/iced, 0–9 m/s); snuff + retract ≤2.5 s.
Reefed launch from the boom tip at 7–14 m/s: success ≥98 %, 50 ms pull ≤20 N, never within 1.3 m of the helmet.
Clothesline / bystander: written resort permission; boom breakaway and crossing-skier tests (impulse ≤2 N·s).
Optic: ≤20 g 4K M12 module with 55–65° HFOV.

envelope.credible: Rider 7–16 m/s, apparent wind ≥7 m/s to launch and ≥4.2 m/s to keep flying; wind 0–9 m/s head/cross and calm (avail 85–90 %), tailwinds degrade (tail-3 ≈80 %, tail-6 ≈55–80 %, tail-9 ≈20–40 %); low-traffic pistes with written permission only (line/boom 0.8–1.3 m above the snow 1 m behind a carving rider); stow while standing only facing the wind.
envelope.requires: L/D ≥≈0.7 unreefed for avail ≥80 % (KE/force/head clearance hold down to 0.6); flying mass ≤≈100 g for avail; active boom pointing ≤≈0.5°; heave-compensating winch ≥7 m/s with ≤30 ms lag.

audit3.basis: 48-case FULLRUN_CASES_R4 on the round-4 shared rules; independent raw-column recompute on 6 spot cases max abs diff 0.04 (setup 2 s rounding)
audit3.summary: All four audit3 majors are addressed by design change, not tolerance: no boom artefact (3 mm passive boom, shared ≥2 px rule), no gimbal motor at all, a real motor envelope with zero violations and passive drag pay-out instead of the ideal heave-compensating winch, noisy sensing. Under the tightened rules avail falls to 72.30 % (FAIL; tailwind band 53.7 %, others 83.5 %) and the clothesline gate still FAILS; the other 12 metrics pass, KE by only 0.62 J.

findings.changed: line/boom height now reported 1, 2 and 3 m behind (min 0.84/0.81/0.74 m; median of case-p10 1.18/1.45/1.70 m; below 1.8 m in 90.2 % of airborne riding samples). Crossing skier: boom 0.20 N·s / 4.0 N (was 1.7 N·s / ≈34 N) thanks to the 25 g free-pivot boom; raised-pole line contact 9.1 N (≤10 N) via radar drag release + 60 ms contact free-spool.

numbers.metric: height above the snow of the boom + line 1, 2 and 3 m (horizontal) behind the boom pivot, every airborne riding sample; lowShare = % of those samples with the lowest of the three below 1.8 m
numbers.target: ≥1.8 m everywhere 1–3 m behind (adult neck/face height, ASSUMED gate from the brief)
numbers.verdict: FAIL: the line/boom is below 1.8 m within 3 m behind the rider for most of the filming time; no exit geometry can hold a ≥1.8 m line near the rider without a rigid member that resists T·Δh (8–14 N·m) and is then ≥2 px wide in the shot

crossingSkier.scenario: neighbour crosses 0.35 m behind at 8 m/s (cross: helmet top 1.9 m; crosspole: pole raised to 2.3 m)
crossingSkier.mechanism: rear radar (4 m, 0.2 s) drops the reel drag to 1.5 N and the kite climbs; a line contact is detected in 60 ms and the solenoid holds free-spool; the 25 g boom is on a free pivot with a 5 N magnetic breakaway (effective struck mass ≤25 g)
